title: Yu Gwan-sun's birth chart
metaDescription: Yu Gwan-sun's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.3° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Sagittarius — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Uranus. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 24.3° Sagittarius — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Sun. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Sagittarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 26.9° Sagittarius, Venus at 28.6° Sagittarius, Mars at 28.6° Virgo. Mercury in a fire sign reads as a mind that decides at speaking speed; Venus in a fire sign reads as taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; Mars in a earth sign reads as drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus to Mars is the closest call of the day, a square within 0.0°. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Mercury square Mars at 1.8°, and Mercury conjunction Venus at 1.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Neptune while both square Mars. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Sagittarius at 26.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Capricorn at 26.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 2 earth, 2 air, 1 water by element and 6 mutable, 2 cardinal, 1 fixed by mode. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 15.1° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
